tagline: Up Willow Creek from the wheat into the Blue Mountains.
intro: The byway leaves I-84 at Heppner Junction and follows Willow Creek southeast on OR 74, past Cecil, where the Oregon Trail crossed the creek, through wheat and canola fields to Ione and Lexington. Both began as sheep stations, and Lexington lost the county seat to Heppner by 33 votes in 1886.

Past Heppner, Willow Creek Road and the Forest Service roads climb into the pine and fir of the Umatilla National Forest, come down into an old lake basin at Ukiah and climb again, ending at the North Fork John Day Campground, where the Elkhorn Drive takes over.
season: TripCheck gives spring and fall as the best time to visit; summer days can be quite hot.

moments.title: Heppner
moments.text: In June 1903 a flash flood down Willow Creek washed away a third of the town's buildings and took 247 lives, and two horsemen outran the water to warn Ione.

moments.title: Ukiah
moments.text: In spring the old lake basin around Ukiah turns bright blue with camas, whose root native people relied on for food.

moments.title: Bridge Creek Wildlife Area
moments.text: A short trail looks over the wintering ground of one of the largest herds of Rocky Mountain elk in the nation, best seen from December through May.

practical: Winter snows close the byway at its higher elevations.
